notes: Perfect claim overlap (C60, C105, C107) regarding TRAF3 dispensability. LLM finds evidence sufficient, but peer reviewers find this 'rather puzzling' given prior independent studies and request investigation of potential clonal variation.

High overlap (C33, C59, C62, C67, C68, C69) on TRAF2/LUBAC redundancy. LLM finds evidence supports functional redundancy, but peer reviewers express concern this 'contradicts with two prior reports' showing negative role for LUBAC and request resolution of discrepancy.

Strong overlap (C37, C84, C85, C86, C87, C99) on NEMO ubiquitin-binding mechanism. Both agree this is well-supported; reviewers explicitly praise demonstration that K63-linked ubiquitin chains sensed by NEMO's ubiquitin-binding domains play predominant role.

Good overlap (C36, C80, C81, C82) on MAVS polymerization requirement for TRAF recruitment. Both accept this mechanistic finding; reviewers implicitly accept as part of well-designed study without raising concerns.

Partial overlap (C31, C56, C57, C61, C103, C104) on TRAF2/5/6 redundancy. Both agree this core finding is well-supported; reviewers state 'evidences provided are quite thorough and complete' for TRAF identification as redundant E3 ligases.

Partial overlap (C71, C72, C74, C75) on TRAF-binding motifs on MAVS. Both accept these findings; reviewers implicitly accept mutagenesis data showing motifs recruit specific TRAFs as part of 'thorough and complete' evidence.

Limited overlap (C5, C6, C7, C34, C78) on MAVS-TRAF interactions. LLM R1 covers broader set of claims about TRAF recruitment; peer R1 encompasses these within larger claim set. Both find evidence supporting TRAF recruitment mechanism.

Minimal overlap (C83) on K63-linked polyubiquitination. LLM finds evidence supports K63 ubiquitin role, but peer reviewers question mechanism, noting 'TRAF2/5 is suggested to have no E3 activity while LUBAC only produces linear chains' and ask how K63 chains are generated without TRAF6.

Limited overlap (C93, C94) on TRAF2 ubiquitination sites. Both express uncertainty: LLM notes redundant target remains unknown; peer reviewers raise 'major concern' about large quantitative differences and request clarification about experimental variations.

Minimal overlap (C32, C58) on TRAF6 E3 ligase activity. LLM R3 focuses specifically on TRAF6 catalytic requirement; peer R1 includes these claims within broader acceptance of TRAF identification. Both find evidence sufficient.

Minimal overlap (C37, C87, C99) on NEMO-ubiquitin interactions. LLM finds NEMO ubiquitin-binding mechanism well-supported; peer R4 questions broader ubiquitination mechanism including how K63 chains are generated, creating partial disagreement on mechanistic details.
Claims C65, C66 on LUBAC dispensability in wild-type cells only appear in LLM results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific finding.
Claims C88, C89, C90, C91 on SILAC mass spectrometry identification of NEMO-associated proteins only appear in LLM results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
Claims C39-C45 on NEMO's IKK-independent role in IRF3 activation only appear in LLM results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this mechanistic finding.
Claims C30, C46, C47 on TRAF6 identification through conventional purification only appear in LLM results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
Claims C100, C101, C102, C38 on overall mechanistic model only appear in LLM results. Peer reviews address individual components but not the integrated model as a whole.
